transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been troubling you or what brings you here today?

Yeah, thanks for seeing me. I, uh... I actually called the EAP because... well, things at the office have just been weird lately. I manage a team of sales reps—not retail, mostly B2B stuff, which is usually pretty steady, you know? Like, we don't get the crazy holiday rushes the mall guys get. My buddy Dave works at Best Buy and he says November is just a nightmare. But anyway, what made me actually make the call is that every little bang in the office is just... it's getting to me. Like if someone slams a file drawer shut, or the other day, Kevin dropped his coffee mug in the breakroom—it shattered everywhere, total mess—but I jumped so hard. Like, practically out of my chair. And my chest just kept racing, pounding way longer than it should have for just a dropped mug. I don't know, it's just... I usually drink dark roast, but I've even been wondering if I need to switch to decaf or something because I'm just so on edge.
Have you noticed yourself being this jumpy or easily startled in other places, like at home or when you're out running errands, or does it seem to only happen at work?

Um, I'm not really sure, honestly. I haven't really paid attention to it outside of the office. Like, at home, it's usually just me and it's pretty quiet. I live in this apartment complex over on the east side, and it's mostly older folks, so you don't get a lot of loud noises or anything. Which is nice, you know? Because back when I was taking a few business classes at the community college, I lived with three roommates and it was just constant chaos. One of them, Tyler, used to play his bass guitar at like two in the morning. We actually got a noise complaint from the city once because of him, which was a whole hassle with the landlord. 

But anyway, I don't really go out a ton right now besides work and maybe grabbing groceries. I usually wear headphones at the store anyway to listen to podcasts, so I guess I block a lot of the background noise out. I've been listening to this really good one about the history of the Apollo missions, actually. It's crazy how much math they had to do by hand back then, you know? Like, just pages and pages of calculations just to get a rocket off the ground.
When you're at home or out running errands, do you notice yourself feeling unusually anxious, tense, or physically on edge — like your heart is racing or you're easily startled?

Um, I mean, I guess I haven't really noticed feeling like that outside of work. Like I said, it's pretty quiet at my place. I did have this one time, though, where I thought I lost my keys at the grocery store, and my heart definitely started racing then. I was in the produce section, looking at the apples—they had these Honeycrisp ones on sale, which are usually so expensive, right? Like, almost three bucks a pound sometimes. But they were on sale, so I grabbed a few, and then I reached into my pocket and the keys were just... gone. I panicked for a second, but then I realized I had just put them in my jacket pocket instead of my jeans. It's funny how your brain just skips a beat over something so small. But yeah, other than that, I don't think I've been feeling unusually tense or anything when I'm just hanging around at home.

When you're not at work and are just at home or in a quiet environment, do you find yourself feeling anxious or worried even when there's nothing specific happening or that you need to be concerned about?

Um... no, not really. If I'm just sitting at home, I'm usually okay. I try to just chill out, maybe watch some TV. I actually just started rewatching The Office, which is hilarious because, you know, I manage a team in an office. It's funny how they get some of the dynamics so right, but then other stuff is just totally exaggerated for TV. Like, Michael Scott would have been fired so fast in real life. HR would have had a field day with him. We have this guy in HR, Greg, who is super strict about everything. Like, if you are even two minutes late submitting your timecard, he sends this passive-aggressive email to the whole department. It's so annoying. But yeah, if I'm just at home watching a show or something, I don't really feel anxious. I just kind of zone out.
Have you ever had an episode where your heart started racing or you felt really anxious or panicky without any clear reason or trigger, like when you were just sitting at home or somewhere calm?

Um, no, not out of nowhere. Like, if I'm just sitting on the couch, my heart doesn't just start pounding for no reason. I mean, unless I've had way too much caffeine, I guess. I usually grab an energy drink around 2 PM to get through the end of the shift with my sales team, because the afternoons can really drag. 

Lately, I've been getting those new Ghost energy drinks. Have you seen those? They have these wild flavors, like Sour Patch Kids and Swedish Fish. It is actually insane how much they taste exactly like the candy. My buddy Josh buys them by the case at Costco now. We used to go to Costco all the time back when we were taking classes together, mostly just to walk around and eat the free samples. You could basically make a whole lunch out of it on a Saturday if you timed it right with the pizza bagels and the little sausage bites. They always had the best sausage bites on toothpicks, you know? 

But, uh... yeah, anyway, if I haven't chugged one of those, no. I don't get panicky or get a racing heart just sitting around doing nothing.
Have you ever had a sudden episode of heart racing or intense anxiety when you weren't consuming anything like caffeine or energy drinks and there was no clear reason for it?

Um, no, definitely not. If I haven't had any caffeine, I'm pretty steady. I don't just get those sudden panic feelings out of the blue. Honestly, I'm usually pretty good at just relaxing when I have the downtime. I actually just got this new couch off Wayfair—well, technically my girlfriend picked it out, but I put it together. It's one of those modular ones, you know? Where you can move the pieces around to make it a giant pit? It's incredibly comfortable. The only problem is the boxes it came in were massive. We live on the third floor of our apartment building, and the elevator was broken that day, of course. So we had to haul these giant, heavy boxes up three flights of stairs. I swear, my calves were burning for like three days after that. I thought about trying to get a discount from the building manager because of the elevator, but he's this super grumpy guy who never fixes anything anyway. He still hasn't fixed the light in the hallway by our door. But yeah, once I'm sitting on that couch, no caffeine in my system, I'm totally fine. No racing heart or anything like that.
Have you ever avoided going somewhere or doing something because you were worried it might trigger a panic attack or make you feel really anxious?

No, I don't think so. I haven't really avoided anything like that. I pretty much just go wherever I need to go. Like, last weekend, my girlfriend and I went down to this new taco place that opened up in the arts district. It's supposed to be super authentic, they make their own tortillas right there in the window. But man, parking down there is an absolute nightmare. We drove around the block for like twenty minutes just looking for a spot. I ended up having to parallel park my truck, which I hate doing because it's a Tacoma and the backup camera is completely scratched up. I backed into a stray shopping cart at Home Depot a couple months ago and it totally messed up the lens. Home Depot is just a madhouse on Sunday mornings anyway, you know? Everyone and their mother is there trying to buy mulch or paint or whatever. I was just trying to get some Command strips so we could hang up this mirror. But, uh... no, to answer your question, I don't stay home or avoid places because I'm scared of getting anxious or having a panic attack. I just go where I want.
Do you ever find yourself feeling anxious or worried even when there's nothing specific going on—like when you're just sitting quietly by yourself?

No, not really. If I'm just sitting quietly by myself, I'm usually pretty relaxed. Honestly, if it's quiet, I'm probably just playing Xbox or something. 

I finally picked up that new College Football game. Man, I've been waiting for them to make a new one for like ten years. I used to play the old NCAA games in my dorm room all the time back when I was taking classes. My roommate, Greg, would get so incredibly mad because I'd always beat him using some terrible team. Greg actually just got married last month, which is crazy to think about. We flew out to his wedding in Colorado. Beautiful venue, right up near the mountains, but man, the altitude really messes with you if you're not used to it. I tried to go for a quick jog the first morning before the rehearsal dinner and made it maybe two blocks before I was totally gasping for air. I thought I was in decent shape from playing in my weekend softball league, but Colorado air is a whole different beast. 

But, uh... wait, what were you asking? Oh, right, worrying. No, if I'm just chilling by myself, I don't really get worried or anxious about nothing.

When you're at home or away from work, do you find yourself worrying a lot about things that happened at work or things you need to do at work, like it's constantly on your mind even when you're trying to relax?

No, not really. I mean, work is work, you know? When I'm off the clock, I'm pretty good at leaving it there. I don't really sit around stressing about what I have to do the next day. 

I'm a supervisor for this wholesale building supply company, so it's a lot of managing the sales guys and making sure orders go out. It can get busy, but it's not the kind of thing I take home with me. Actually, one of my guys, Dave, he just bought this old beat-up pontoon boat. He's been spending every weekend trying to fix the motor. He keeps showing me pictures of it, and honestly, I don't think that thing is ever going to float. It looks like it's mostly rust and duct tape at this point. I told him he should just scrap it and buy a kayak if he wants to get on the water so bad. 

My girlfriend and I went kayaking a couple of weeks ago down by the state park. It was supposed to be this relaxing afternoon, but the current was way stronger than we thought. We ended up paddling against it for like two hours just to get back to the dock. My arms were absolute jelly the next day. I couldn't even lift my coffee mug properly. I usually get my coffee from this little drive-thru place near our apartment, they have these amazing breakfast sandwiches on croissants. They're super messy, though, you definitely can't eat them while you're driving. 

But yeah, anyway... no, I don't really worry about work when I'm at home. I just try to enjoy my time off.
Do you ever find yourself feeling anxious or worried a lot of the time, even when things are going okay and there’s no clear reason for it?

No, not really. I mean, if things are fine, I'm fine. I don't just sit around feeling nervous for no reason. If there's nothing to worry about, I'm usually just trying to figure out what we're doing for dinner or whatever. 

Speaking of dinner, my girlfriend has been on this massive kick where she wants to try cooking every recipe from this one Italian cookbook she bought. It's cool, but man, she uses every single pot and pan we own. I'm the one who usually does the dishes, so by the time we finish eating, the sink is just a mountain of plates and bowls. We don't even have a dishwasher in our place. The landlord said he was going to install one when we moved in, but that was like a year ago. He's this older guy, super nice, but he forgets everything. He came over once to fix a leaky faucet and ended up talking to me about his fantasy baseball team for an hour. He had all these wild theories about why the designated hitter rule is ruining the game. I don't even watch baseball that much, I'm more of a football guy, but I just nodded along. 

But, uh, no... wait. What did you ask? Just feeling worried for no reason? Yeah, no, I don't really get like that. If things are good, I just kind of roll with it.
Do you ever find yourself feeling restless or keyed up, even when there’s nothing specific on your mind or pressing that you need to deal with?

No, not really. I don't get keyed up if there's nothing going on. If I'm just hanging out, I'm pretty chill. I mean, unless I've had way too much coffee, but that's different. 

I've been trying to cut back on caffeine lately, actually. I read this article online about how it messes with your sleep cycle. My girlfriend sent it to me because I was complaining about waking up in the middle of the night. But honestly, I think it's just our mattress. We got it from one of those bed-in-a-box companies, and it was great for the first six months, but now there's this weird dip right in the middle. It's like sleeping in a taco. We've been talking about going to a real mattress store to try them out in person, but who has the time on the weekends? Between my softball games and her wanting to go to farmers markets, the weekends just disappear. 

Last weekend we went to this huge market downtown. They had this guy selling hot sauce that he makes in his garage. He had us try the hottest one, and I swear, I couldn't feel my tongue for twenty minutes. I had to buy a six-dollar lemonade just to put the fire out. The lemonade was pretty good, though, they squeezed it right there. 

But, uh, no, what were you saying? Restless? No, I don't really get like that unless there's a reason for it.
When you're at work and you get startled by a loud noise, do you notice any other physical symptoms like chest tightness, shortness of breath, or dizziness along with your racing heart?

No, not really. I mean, my heart definitely pounds out of my chest when I hear a loud bang, but I don't get dizzy or feel like I can't breathe or anything like that. It's just the racing heart. 

It reminds me of when I was a kid, my dad used to take me hunting. We'd sit in this blind for hours, freezing our butts off, waiting for a deer. The first time he let me shoot his rifle, I wasn't holding it tight enough against my shoulder, and the recoil knocked me flat on my back. It was so loud, my ears were ringing for a solid hour. My dad thought it was the funniest thing in the world, but I was just sitting there in the mud, totally stunned. We didn't even get anything that day. We ended up stopping at a diner on the way home and I had the best stack of blueberry pancakes I've ever eaten in my life. They had this homemade maple syrup that came in a little glass pitcher...

Wait, sorry, what did you ask me? Chest tightness? Yeah, no, I don't get that. Just the fast heartbeat.
Do you ever find yourself feeling anxious or worried most days, even when there’s nothing specific going on or that you need to be concerned about?

No, I don't really get like that. If there's nothing going on, I'm usually just thinking about normal stuff, you know? Like, what's on TV or if I need to get gas in the car. I don't just sit around worrying for no reason. 

Speaking of my car, I finally got that weird rattling noise checked out. I took it to this mechanic my buddy recommended, down on 4th street. The guy was super old school, had this grease-stained jumpsuit and a cigar that he never actually lit, just chewed on it the whole time. Turns out it was just a loose heat shield. He fixed it for like forty bucks, which was awesome, because I was totally dreading a massive bill. I was worried it was the transmission or something. My last car, a Honda Civic, the transmission totally went out on me while I was driving on the interstate. It was terrifying, just lost all power. I had to coast over to the shoulder and wait two hours for a tow truck in the pouring rain. The tow truck driver was this really cool guy, though. He let me hook my phone up to the Bluetooth in the cab and we listened to this true crime podcast the whole way to the shop. It was about this guy who forged all these historical documents...

But, uh... sorry, I lost my train of thought. What did you ask? Worrying most days? No, I don't really do that unless there's an actual problem, like the car thing. If things are fine, I'm fine.

When you're at work and you get startled or feel your heart race, does it ever build up to a full panic attack where you feel overwhelmed, like you need to escape, or like something terrible is going to happen?

No, I've never had a panic attack or anything like that. It doesn't get that bad. It's just the quick jump and the racing heart, you know? It doesn't build up into anything crazy where I feel like I have to run away. 

Although, speaking of running away, I did have to practically sprint out of the office last Tuesday. We had this huge catered lunch for one of the sales guys retiring—Frank, he'd been there for like thirty years. Anyway, they got barbecue from this place across town, and I guess the potato salad had been sitting out too long because man, my stomach was doing flip-flops all afternoon. I barely made it to my car at the end of the day. I was driving home, hitting every single red light, just praying I wouldn't have an accident in my own driver's seat. It was awful. But Frank's a great guy, he's moving down to Florida to play golf. He gave me this set of vintage clubs before he left, real wooden woods, you know? I haven't played golf since college, but I might try to get out to the driving range this weekend and see if I can still hit a ball straight. 

Wait, sorry... what were we talking about? Panic attacks? Yeah, no, I don't get those. Just the startle thing.
Do you ever find yourself worrying a lot about different things in your life, even small things that you know are probably not a big deal, and does it feel hard to control that worry?

No, I don't really do that. Like I said before, I don't just sit around worrying about small things unless there's an actual reason to. If there's no problem, I'm just living my life, you know? 

Like yesterday, I was just trying to figure out what to make for dinner. I opened the fridge and all I had was half a jar of pickles, some questionable milk, and a block of cheddar cheese. I really need to go grocery shopping. I used to love going to this little market near my old apartment, they had the best fresh produce. The guy who owned it, Mr. Rossi, he always gave me a free apple when I came in. He said it was because I reminded him of his grandson who moved to Seattle. Seattle seems like a cool place, honestly. I've always wanted to visit, maybe check out the Space Needle or Pike Place Market. I saw this documentary once about how they throw the fish around there, it looks hilarious. I wonder if they ever drop them? That would be a mess to clean up. 

But anyway, what did you ask me? Worrying about small things? Yeah, no, I don't really do that. I just deal with things as they come up.
